findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 3a9059f9de3c9bdc412a79e87c225f378eb8390109bb29e4760951d9f4970181; all 6 declared sources passed current access review.

Claims remain bounded to MRX directional-assessment scope, professional appraisal-standards context, mineral-ownership research complexity, and the RRC GIS non-authoritative-data limitation. No source is converted into private title, an appraiser-prepared value opinion, reserves, offer terms, owner net, legal or tax treatment, or transaction advice.

The article invents no real owner, property, buyer, contract, transaction, price range, production, reserves, forecast, testimonial, success rate, or owner-specific legal, tax, accounting, title, appraisal, engineering, investment, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology describes a directional range with stated evidence, assumptions, scenarios, and professional limits rather than a teaser number or certified valuation.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to define the inspectable fields and limits of a directional assessment; it does not establish title, reserves, certified value, legal or tax treatment, an offer, expected owner net, or a sell decision.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Frequently Asked Questions (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX FAQ describes the service as a directional underwriter assessment and distinguishes it from a certified valuation, legal opinion, or tax opinion.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only for first-party scope language and professional referrals; it does not establish owner-specific title, value, taxes, suitability, an offer, payment, closing, or a sell-versus-hold recommendation.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Terms and AI Disclosure (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX terms state that public content is educational and is not a certified appraisal, title opinion, reserve certification, or individualized professional conclusion.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to preserve service and content limitations; it does not derive owner-specific legal, tax, title, appraisal, reserves, engineering, value, offer, or transaction conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: The Appraisal Foundation, Appraisal Standards and Qualifications (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Appraisal Foundation maintains recognized ethical and performance standards for the appraisal profession in the United States and identifies appraisal disciplines addressed by those standards.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to distinguish MRX directional assessment scope from an appraisal engagement; it does not claim that the source determines a specific engagement, credential, jurisdictional requirement, or owner-specific value.

sources_inspected.label: Texas A&M AgriLife, How Do I Find Out If I Own Mineral Rights? (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas A&M AgriLife explains that mineral ownership may be severed or divided and that chain-of-title research can be complex and difficult even for experienced oil-and-gas attorneys.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to explain why a directional assessment cannot substitute for chain-of-title work; it does not decide ownership, acreage, deed meaning, legal rights, value, or a transaction result.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Public GIS Viewer (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas says its Public GIS Viewer datasets are informational, may not be suitable for legal, engineering, or surveying purposes, are not authoritative geographic records, and have no legal force or effect.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to bound map and identifier context; it does not treat the viewer as a title record, legal boundary, acreage proof, reserves conclusion, private ownership evidence, value, or transaction advice.
